comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations set out a common first year, a 40 EC specialisation, a 30 EC minor and a 20 EC Integration Project. Production Technology and Logistics is the first of two specialisations listed.

routeSelection.basis: The generic IEM target has two formally named, equal-sized specialisations and current official evidence does not establish either as more representative or general. The first-listed specialisation in the 2026-2027 appendix is therefore selected neutrally, without regard to UCR fit.

core: Industrial and organisational systems, process improvement and integrated technical-business decisions
Mathematics, programming, statistics, modelling, simulation and optimisation
Business economics, accounting, marketing, organisations, strategy and entrepreneurship
Production, logistics, supply chains, engineering design, manufacturing and quality control
adjacent: Sustainable production, renewable energy, lifecycle analysis and circular resource systems
Technology entrepreneurship, digital transformation and evidence-led product innovation
questions: How can models, data and optimisation improve industrial and organisational decisions?
How can innovation be evaluated and designed for technical, economic and environmental feasibility?

candidates.label: Sustainable production, energy and circular resources
Technology entrepreneurship and product design
candidates.reason: The completed closest programme already gives entrepreneurship, product design, strategy, market research and technical-economic assessment a substantial role. A third route would reorganise many of the same business and design courses rather than create a genuinely different 24-course curriculum.

selection.assessment: The first option combines business, computation and systems modelling. The second concentrates on energy and material flows, recovery and technical and economic assessment. Product development and digital strategy already have a place in the first option. A separate manufacturing pathway would require a deeper sequence in mechanics, CAD, production and industrial controls.

alternatives.label: Industrial decisions, data & organisational systems
alternatives.labelReason: Systems modelling and computation support decisions about products, strategy and organisations.
alternatives.concept: Use mathematics, programming and evidence to study how organisations make decisions about products and technology. Model signals and feedback, programme a robot arm, and apply optimisation and market research to design and business questions.
progression: Programming and mathematical methods precede linear algebra, robotics, signals, algorithms and optimisation. Introductory economics and research methods precede econometrics.

alternatives.label: Sustainable production, energy & circular resources
alternatives.labelReason: Life-cycle assessment, resource recovery and renewable-energy design are the core applications, supported by quantitative, financial and policy work.
alternatives.concept: Study how products use energy and materials, and how those resources can be recovered and reused. Combine life-cycle assessment, recycling experiments and renewable-energy design with numerical modelling, costing and policy analysis.
progression: Sustainability gateways precede applied geochemistry, resources and renewable design. Energy & Sustainability precedes Renewable System Design. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, probability and numerical modelling.
alternatives.distinctness: Fourteen courses, or 105 EC, differ in each direction. The second programme replaces advanced organisational, economics, marketing, communication, database, machine-learning, deep-learning, algorithm and optimisation study with lifecycle analysis, Earth-system tools, soils and aquifers, biogeochemistry, recovery, resources, renewable-system design and sustainability governance. These are curricular consequences of the sustainable-process and energy evidence, not threshold-filling substitutions.

notes.text: The UCR options cover parts of industrial decision-making, systems modelling and sustainable design. Groningen adds a specialist sequence in mechanics, manufacturing, CAD, control engineering and production planning, and requires a 20 EC Integration Project.

blocks: Both teach programming for modelling and problem-solving; UCR is general Python and computational reasoning rather than an industrial simulation sequence.
Both develop single-variable calculus, including differentiation and integration. UCR also uses complex numbers and differential equations to model dynamic systems.
Both directly study linear algebra, matrices, vector spaces and transformations.
Both develop probability and statistics; UCR is a general mathematical course rather than industrial stochastic modelling.
Both formulate and solve optimisation problems with objectives and constraints, including linear programming. Groningen also covers transport, assignment and network-flow problems.
Both model continuous and discrete signals and linear systems using differential equations, Fourier methods, convolution and filtering. UCR also introduces feedback.
Both use costs, budgets and performance measures to support management decisions. UCR also covers financial statements and investment appraisal.
Both study organisational behaviour, motivation, leadership and group dynamics.
Both develop a design through problem definition, research and prototyping. UCR focuses on consumer products. Groningen investigates complex engineering systems.
Both address innovation strategy and implementation; UCR emphasises digital transformation and responsible value creation.
Both examine market evidence and customer response; UCR focuses on market research rather than industrial marketing as a complete field.
UCR introduces physics, chemistry and materials foundations for sustainability, but not the external course’s materials-and-molecules depth.
Specialist engineering, minor and final project

audience.programmeDescription: Industrial Engineering and Management at the University of Groningen combines mathematics and engineering with business. In Production Technology and Logistics, students study manufacturing, signals, control and production planning, then complete a supervised integration project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One UCR option combines business decisions with modelling and robotics. The other studies renewable energy, material recovery and life-cycle assessment. Groningen offers more depth in engineering design, manufacturing and industrial logistics.
